response.sql: WITH pairs AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, u.acctscope AS acctscope, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope HAVING AVG(f.feerate) IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS mean_avg FROM pairs), kept AS (SELECT p.orderslink, p.acctscope, p.avg_rate, p.avg_rate - o.mean_avg AS excess FROM pairs p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_rate > o.mean_avg), ranked AS (SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_rate, excess, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY acctscope ORDER BY excess DESC, orderslink ASC) AS rnk FROM kept) SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_rate, excess, rnk FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 3 ORDER BY acctscope, rnk

assumptions.assumption: Pairs whose feerate values are all NULL have no average and are excluded from the pair set, so they do not count toward the overall mean of pair averages.
The overall mean is the unweighted mean of the pair averages (each pair counts once), computed over all pairs before filtering.
If orders.recordvault or users.userstamp has duplicates, joined rows are all kept and contribute to the averages.
